_meta.basis: Monthly costs for a single remote worker living mid-range: private 1BR apartment in a central/nomad-popular area, cooking ~half of meals, one coworking hot desk, local transport, mobile data.
_meta.confidence: Seed estimates for MVP. Every figure must display a 'last verified' date in the UI. Visa and tax fields are informational only, never advice.

visa_rule_types.SCHENGEN_90_180: Rolling window. Max 90 days in any trailing 180-day period across the whole Schengen Area combined. Entry day and exit day both count. No reset by leaving to a non-Schengen country.
visa_rule_types.FIXED_PER_ENTRY: A fresh allowance each time you enter. Border runs may reset it, but repeated same-day runs draw scrutiny.
visa_rule_types.ROLLING_PER_YEAR: Max N days per rolling 12 months or per calendar year, tracked cumulatively.
visa_rule_types.NOMAD_VISA: A dedicated remote-work residence permit. Separate from tourist allowance.

nomadVisa.name: D8 Digital Nomad Visa
nomadVisa.notes: Requires ~4x Portuguese minimum wage in monthly income, proof of remote contract or freelance clients, NIF number, and Portuguese bank account.

tax.notes: The old NHR regime closed to new entrants; a narrower successor (IFICI) targets scientific and high-value activity. Assume standard progressive rates unless you qualify.

cities.arbitrageNote: Prices rose sharply 2022-2026. Still strong for the infrastructure, but no longer the bargain it was.

nomadVisa.name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
nomadVisa.notes: 5-year multi-entry. Each entry allows 180 days, extendable once by 180 more (up to 360 consecutive days). Requires 500,000 THB held for at least 3 months — recent large deposits and crypto transfers are red flags. Must be applied for from outside Thailand.

tax.notes: 180+ days in a calendar year makes you Thai tax resident. Since 2024 Thailand taxes foreign income remitted into Thailand by residents. Remittance timing matters.

cities.arbitrageNote: Best cost-to-infrastructure ratio on this list. Burning season (Feb-Apr) is a real air-quality problem; plan around it.

tax.notes: Same remittance-basis rules as Chiang Mai.

cities.arbitrageNote: World-class transit, hospitals and airport connectivity for under half of Western European cost.

nomadVisa.name: Temporary Resident Visa (economic solvency)
nomadVisa.notes: Not branded a nomad visa but functions as one. Must be applied for at a Mexican consulate abroad, not inside Mexico. Thresholds are pegged to Mexican minimum wage and move annually.

tax.notes: Day count is one test; having your 'centre of vital interests' in Mexico can trigger residency independently.

cities.arbitrageNote: Border officers increasingly grant less than 180 days at their discretion. Do not assume the full stamp.

nomadVisa.name: V-Visa Digital Nomad
nomadVisa.notes: Among the lowest income thresholds worldwide (roughly 3x Colombian minimum wage). Does not count toward permanent residency.

tax.windowNote: 183 days across any rolling 365-day period, which can straddle two tax years.
tax.notes: Colombian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income. This catches long-stay nomads more often than they expect.

cities.arbitrageNote: Year-round spring climate, strong founder scene in El Poblado and Laureles. Petty crime and drink-spiking are genuine risks; the app should surface safety guidance, not hide it.

tax.notes: Currency and capital-control regime has been volatile; verify the current FX situation before committing to a long lease.

cities.arbitrageNote: Costs swing hard with the peso. Highly volatile — treat these figures as low-confidence and refresh often.

nomadVisa.name: E33G Remote Worker KITAS
nomadVisa.notes: Requires proof of employment or contracts with a company outside Indonesia. Income from Indonesian sources is not permitted.

tax.notes: E33G holders are generally not taxed on foreign-sourced income, but crossing 183 days on other visa types can trigger residency.

cities.arbitrageNote: Internet is the weak point — always verify actual speeds at the specific villa, not the island average. Scooter accidents are the top health risk; insurance often excludes them without a local licence.

nomadVisa.name: Remotely from Georgia
nomadVisa.notes: Largely redundant given the 365-day visa-free stay for 90+ nationalities.

tax.notes: Small Business Status offers 1% tax on turnover up to 500,000 GEL/yr (~USD 180k) for registered individual entrepreneurs. Turnover above the cap is taxed at 3%. This is the single biggest tax arbitrage on this list for freelancers.

cities.arbitrageNote: 365 days visa-free plus a 1% freelancer tax regime is the strongest combined visa+tax play available. Banking has become harder for some nationalities — verify before relying on it.

tax.notes: Flat 15% personal income tax. White Card holders are generally not permitted to work for Hungarian companies.

cities.arbitrageNote: Cheapest EU capital with genuinely good infrastructure. Schengen clock applies.

nomadVisa.name: Digital Nomad residence permit
nomadVisa.notes: Non-Schengen, so time here does not burn Schengen days.

tax.notes: Serbia offers a foreign-income exemption for qualifying nomads in the first 90 days. Non-Schengen status makes it a useful 'reset' base between EU stints.

cities.arbitrageNote: Prime Schengen-clock parking spot. Cheap, in the European timezone, and days spent here do not count against your 90/180.

tax.notes: High inflation environment; local-currency figures go stale fast.

cities.arbitrageNote: Non-Schengen with a major airline hub. Inflation makes cost data unusually volatile — refresh monthly.

nomadVisa.name: None dedicated
nomadVisa.notes: No dedicated nomad visa. Freelancers typically use the national D-visa or B2B self-employment route.

tax.notes: Registered sole traders can access a lump-sum 12-15% IT services rate, which is attractive for developers.

cities.arbitrageNote: Best internet and safety per dollar in the EU. Strong startup and developer talent pool for founder collaboration.

nomadVisa.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Highly Qualified Employees programme)
nomadVisa.notes: Limited to nationals of a specific eligible list, IT/tech focused.

tax.notes: The 'živnostenský list' trade licence with the 60/40 flat expense deduction is a long-standing freelancer play.

cities.arbitrageNote: Very walkable, excellent transit, mature freelancer legal framework.

nomadVisa.name: Visado de Teletrabajo Internacional
nomadVisa.notes: Roughly 200% of Spanish SMI. Freelancers may earn no more than 20% of income from Spanish clients.

tax.notes: Nomad visa holders may apply for the Beckham Law regime: flat 24% on Spanish-source income up to EUR 600k for up to 6 years. Canary Islands also have reduced IGIC (7%) instead of mainland VAT (21%).

cities.arbitrageNote: Best year-round climate in the EU, and the Beckham Law makes Spain unusually attractive for high earners despite headline rates.

tax.notes: 50% income tax exemption for 7 years for qualifying new tax residents who commit to staying 2+ years.

cities.arbitrageNote: Cheapest Eurozone capital with a real nomad scene. Summer heat is increasingly severe.

nomadVisa.name: Digital Nomad Visa (Type D)
nomadVisa.notes: The world's first dedicated nomad visa (2020). Income threshold is gross, and high.

tax.notes: e-Residency lets you run an EU company remotely, but it grants no residency, no visa, and does not change your personal tax residence. Widely misunderstood.

cities.arbitrageNote: Best digital government on earth. Public transport is free for residents. Winter darkness is a real quality-of-life factor.

tax.notes: 0% personal income tax. 9% corporate tax applies above AED 375k profit.

cities.arbitrageNote: Expensive to live, but 0% income tax flips the arbitrage math entirely above roughly USD 120k/yr. The calculator must model post-tax income, not just cost of living.

nomadVisa.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass
nomadVisa.notes: Restricted to IT, digital marketing, content and similar digital professions.

tax.notes: Foreign-sourced income remitted to Malaysia is exempt for individuals through at least 2026 — verify the current sunset date.

cities.arbitrageNote: Most underrated on this list: English-speaking, great internet, cheap, good healthcare, major airport hub. Weak nomad social scene compared to Bali or Chiang Mai.

nomadVisa.name: None dedicated
nomadVisa.notes: No nomad visa. The 90-day e-visa (single or multiple entry) is the practical route.

tax.notes: Residents taxed on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 35%. Enforcement against foreigners has historically been light but is tightening.

cities.arbitrageNote: 90-day e-visa is generous and easy. Air quality and traffic noise are the main complaints.

nomadVisa.name: Employment Gold Card
nomadVisa.notes: Combines work permit, residence visa, ARC and re-entry permit in one.

tax.notes: Gold Card holders get a 50% exemption on income over TWD 3m for the first 5 years of residency.

cities.arbitrageNote: Safest city on this list, world-class transit and internet. The Gold Card is one of the best-value long-term nomad permits anywhere.

nomadVisa.name: Workation Visa (F-1-D)
nomadVisa.notes: Requires income of at least twice Korea's GNI per capita and 1+ year with the same employer.

tax.notes: Progressive rates up to 45%. High income threshold on the visa means most holders are exposed.

cities.arbitrageNote: Fastest internet on the list. High income bar and weak English make it a specialist choice.

nomadVisa.name: Remote Work Visa
nomadVisa.notes: Holders staying under 6 months in a 12-month window are exempt from SA income tax registration.

tax.notes: NON-CALENDAR TAX YEAR: 1 March to 28/29 February. Also uses a separate 'ordinarily resident' test. Day-count alone is not the whole picture.

cities.arbitrageNote: Extraordinary scenery and value in the European timezone, but violent crime rates are genuinely high and load-shedding can disrupt work. Do not soften this in the UI.

nomadVisa.name: Premium Travel Visa
nomadVisa.notes: Free to apply. One of the easiest approvals on this list.

tax.notes: NON-CALENDAR TAX YEAR: 1 July to 30 June. Flat 15% income tax; foreign income not remitted to Mauritius is generally not taxed.

cities.arbitrageNote: Free visa, 15% flat tax, English-speaking, safe. Isolated and car-dependent; flights are expensive.

nomadVisa.name: Unique Permit for Digital Nomads
nomadVisa.notes: Very low income threshold. 1-year visa-free stay for US citizens makes the permit optional for many.

tax.notes: Nomad permit holders have been granted a foreign-income exemption in the first year. Verify current status before relying on it.

cities.arbitrageNote: Non-Schengen, dirt cheap, 365-day visa-free for US passports, on the Adriatic. The dark horse of European arbitrage.

tax.notes: Same as Mexico City.

cities.arbitrageNote: Caribbean beach plus a real nomad scene, US timezone overlap. Sargassum season (Apr-Aug) and humidity are the trade-offs.
